title: Shortcut not working despite no detected conflicts

judgment.rationale: Use the existing dedicated-keyboard-thread work for the hook-reliability portion. Keep conflict-reporting expectations distinct from successful system-shortcut interception; do not promise #50982 resolves every warning/UI expectation.
evidence: Without the low-level hook, Win+S opens Windows Search; with the hook, both applications sometimes open.
The maintainer says the hook is required for system-shortcut override and points to #50982 for reliability.
A 'no conflict' UI result is not proof that Windows does not reserve a shortcut.

The reporter says an AutoHotkey remap from Win+S to the ordinary CmdPal shortcut works, while the PowerToys hook still does not. A maintainer notes AHK uses the same low-level hook mechanism; that does not prove equivalent thread/lifetime behavior.

initial_investigation: Read open #50982's GlobalHotkeyService/GlobalKeyboardHook changes: hooks run on a dedicated message loop with renewal and nonblocking callback requirements.

Read all three new replies. Covering dedicated-keyboard-thread PR50982 is still open and unmerged, so no shipped-fix claim is made. Retained maintainer reproduction rather than asking for another generic report.

reproduce.title: Validate Command Palette hotkeys report
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable release; compare the reported version only in an isolated test environment if needed.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: Set Win+S, compare hook disabled/enabled and a nonreserved shortcut.
Compare current stable with the existing #50982 branch in a controlled environment and verify both activation and suppression of Windows Search.
Record conflict diagnostics separately from hook interception behavior.

Compare the reported AHK Win+S-to-default-shortcut workaround with the same direct CmdPal Win+S binding; record which application receives the key-up/down events without logging unrelated typed input.
reproduce.expected_result: The hook-enabled override activates only the intended target; any remaining conflict-display limitation is identified separately.
